newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE Australia cotton crop f'cast 606,000 T.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE Australia cotton crop f'cast 606,000 T.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) has increased its forecast of Australia's 1996/97 (July-June) cotton crop to a record 606,000 tonnes and is predicting further gains next year.

The 1996/97 forecast, contained in ABARE's Australian Crop Report released on Tuesday, is up from ABARE's 552,000 tonne forecast in March and compares with the 421,000 tonnes produced in 1995/96. The 1996/97 cotton harvest is almost complete, with less than five percent of the crop left to harvest, ABARE said.
Forecast production for 1997/98 has been set at 607,000 tonnes, slightly ahead of 1996/97.
The estimated crop of 606,000 tonnes, or 2.67 million 500-pound bales, would break the 1991/92 record of 2.2 million bales, said ABARE, the government's main commodities forecaster.
"Ideal harvest conditions and favourable weather conditions throughout most of the growing season have resulted in average or above average yields for the 1996/97 crop," ABARE said.
However, rainfall late in the season was expected to result in a reduction in quality through discolouring of up to 10 percent of the cotton crop, ABARE said.
Total cotton plantings are forecast at 417,000 hectares for 1997/98, up from 408,000 hectares in 1996/97.

The major dams serving the main northern summer cropping regions were at an average capacity of 81 percent and few areas were expected to have restrictions placed on their water allocation for 1997/98, ABARE said.
Irrigated plantings in 1997/98 are forecast to be about the same as the 1996/97 area, given anticipated water allocations.
